subject: general
question: Who succeeded Dhruvasena?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dharapatta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dharapatta succeeded Dhruvasena Baladitya II, who was a ruler of the Maitraka dynasty in Gujarat.
 
• The Maitraka dynasty was established in the 5th century CE and ruled western India with Vallabhi (modern-day Gujarat) as its capital.
 
• Dharapatta continued the legacy of the Maitraka rulers, known for their contributions to education and administration in the region.
 
• The Maitraka rulers were followers of Buddhism and Hinduism, and Dharapatta, like his predecessors, played a significant role in promoting these religions.
 
• The dynasty's decline began with the invasions by Arabs and other external forces in the 8th century CE.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maitraka Dynasty**

 
 
• The Maitraka dynasty ruled Gujarat and parts of western India between the 5th and 8th centuries CE.
 
• They were originally vassals of the Gupta Empire before declaring independence.
 
• The dynasty is known for establishing Vallabhi University, a renowned center of learning during its time.
 
 
 
• **Dhruvasena Baladitya II**
 
 
• Dhruvasena Baladitya II was one of the prominent rulers of the Maitraka dynasty.
 
• He was known for his administrative capabilities and patronage of Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Vallabhi University**
 
 
• Vallabhi University was an ancient center of learning during the Maitraka period.
 
• It attracted scholars from across India and was considered on par with Nalanda University.
 
 
 
• **Arab Invasions**
 
 
• The decline of the Maitraka dynasty was hastened by invasions from Arab forces.
 
• These invasions disrupted the stability and administration of the region.
